name: Self-counting knee implant
subtitle: a battery-free knee that counts its bends

effects.effect: a treated wire flips its magnetism suddenly and gives a sharp pulse

effect: a treated wire flips its magnetism suddenly and gives a sharp pulse
how: Knee replacements wear out after enough millions of steps, but surgeons can only guess how hard each patient uses theirs and spot the wear late on X-rays. A treated wire in one half of the implant and a small magnet in the other flip the wire's magnetism at every bend, and the sharp pulse powers a counter chip for an instant; a wand held over the knee reads the tally, with no battery ever to replace.
obstacle: Fitting the wire and its pickup coil inside a metal implant without the surrounding metal smothering the magnetic flip.
why: Battery-free pulse counting is proven in water meters; inside a metal joint it isn't.
real: A patent describes a joint-implant cycle counter with a magnet in one component and a Hall switch in the other counting flexion steps (US7347874); Wiegand wires are marketed for implants, but no Wiegand knee counter exists.
